sights.address: 118 Nguyen Van Thu, Dakao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: Ho Chi Minh City's leading contemporary commercial gallery (founded 2003), a four-floor 600 sqm space showing serious Vietnamese and international artists. The best single stop to gauge the city's contemporary art scene; Tue-Sat, free.

sights.address: 6D Ngo Thoi Nhiem, Ward 7, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A heritage-and-arts house-museum in a historic District 3 villa, founded by collector John Tue Nguyen as a hub for Vietnamese art and culture with a specialist library. Exhibitions plus salon events; Tuesdays open, other days by appointment.

sights.address: 27i Tran Nhat Duat, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: One of Saigon's longest-running commercial galleries (est. 2009), known for championing emerging and mid-career Vietnamese painters. A reliable window on contemporary local painting away from the tourist trail.

sights.address: 48/7 Me Linh, Ward 19, Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: Vietnam's most influential artist-run nonprofit (founded 2007 by Dinh Q Le and others), running exhibitions, talks and a residency program. The intellectual engine of the country's independent contemporary art; check current location/programming before visiting as it relocates periodically.

sights.address: 1057 Binh Quoi, Ward 28, Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: An artist-run experimental art space on the leafy Binh Quoi peninsula, hosting installations, performances, sound events and open studios. A destination for the city's more avant-garde, non-commercial art.

sights.address: 15 Nguyen U Di, Thao Dien Ward, District 2 (Thu Duc City), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: Vietnam's first purpose-built independent contemporary arts centre (opened 2016 in Thao Dien), with gallery halls, a cafe/bar and design shop. The anchor of the Thao Dien art cluster; confirm current programming/hours before going.

sights.n: Ao Dai Museum (Bao Tang Ao Dai)
sights.address: 206/19/30 Long Thuan, Long Phuoc Ward, District 9 (Thu Duc City), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A garden-house museum by designer Si Hoang tracing the evolution of Vietnam's national dress, the ao dai, through centuries of examples. A tranquil riverside garden setting ~22 km east of the centre; daily 09:00-18:00, ~100,000d.

sights.address: 870 Truong Sa, Ward 14, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A near-century-old pagoda on the Nhieu Loc Canal, a city-designated heritage site and the city's most photogenic Vesak venue, when thousands of lanterns are floated on the water. Serene canal-side visit any day; spectacular at Buddha's Birthday (4th lunar month).

sights.address: 1408 Duong 3 Thang 2, Ward 2, District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: An early-19th-century pagoda built on the foundations of an ancient Khmer/Oc Eo-era temple mound, a recognised National Historical-Cultural Monument with a fine timber-framed Southern-style hall. A quiet, deeply historic stop in District 11.

sights.address: 161/85/20 Lac Long Quan, Ward 3, District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A 1789 pagoda (sister to Giac Lam) once patronised by Emperor Gia Long, a National Historical-Cultural Relic preserving over 150 antique statues and classic Southern Vietnamese temple carving. Atmospheric and rarely crowded, tucked beside Dam Sen.

sights.address: 120 Tran Binh Trong, Ward 2, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The oldest Catholic parish in the city (origins to 1722; present Gothic-Revival church inaugurated 1896), with soaring stone columns, red-tile roof and a climbable bell tower. A monumental, little-touristed church in the Cho Lon area.

sights.address: Pham Ngu Lao, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A long, 9-hectare downtown green ribbon on the site of Saigon's demolished 19th-century railway station, running from behind Ben Thanh Market through the backpacker quarter. Handy central breathing space for a stroll or people-watching.

sights.address: Dien Bien Phu, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A shaded central park laid out in 1983 over the former Massiges (European) Cemetery, once the resting place of colonial elites and President Ngo Dinh Diem. A leafy escape with a fascinating buried history documented by Saigoneer.

sights.address: 10B Ton Duc Thang, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The 1.3 km riverside park and pier on the Saigon River where locals gather at sunset and river cruises and the 15,000d public waterbus depart for Thu Duc. The best way to see the city from the water, past Landmark 81 and Bitexco.

sights.address: 141 Bach Dang, Ward 2, Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A sprawling 1942 wet-and-wares market that is the beating heart of Binh Thanh, next to the Le Van Duyet tomb, with a lively street-food night market spilling out after dark. An authentic, tourist-light local market.

sights.address: 07 Cong Truong Lam Son, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The signature 'bamboo circus' by Lune Production staged in the colonial Saigon Opera House, blending acrobatics, contemporary dance and live folk music into a rural-to-urban Vietnamese story. The city's marquee cultural show (~1 hour, nightly).

sights.address: 55B Nguyen Thi Minh Khai, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The city's main venue for mua roi nuoc (water puppetry), the thousand-year-old northern folk art performed on a pool of water with live traditional musicians. Two short shows daily (17:00 and 18:30) beside Tao Dan Park.

sights.address: Le Cong Kieu, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A 200 m lane near Ben Thanh (the former Rue de Reims) packed with dozens of antique and curio shops selling colonial memorabilia, old coins, ceramics, watches and reproductions. A browsable slice of old Saigon; haggle hard.

sights.address: 34-36 An Duong Vuong, Ward 9, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A 70-year-old, four-storey wholesale market on the edge of Cho Lon and the city's largest fashion bazaar, plus a famously good basement food court and dried-goods hall. Grittier and cheaper than Ben Thanh; a real trading experience.

sights.n: Ton That Dam Old Market (Cho Cu)
sights.address: Ton That Dam, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: Saigon's original 'old market', a one-block street bazaar of produce, meat and liquor that was once the city's premier source of imported goods before Ben Thanh was built. A raw, fast-vanishing pocket of downtown history documented by Saigoneer.

sights.n: Hai Thuong Lan Ong Traditional Medicine Street
sights.address: Hai Thuong Lan Ong, Ward 10, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A ~1 km Cho Lon street lined with 60-80 traditional-medicine shops, the oldest and largest herbal district in the city, its air thick with cinnamon, star anise, ginseng and dried herbs. A sensory heritage walk named for the father of Vietnamese medicine.

sights.address: 14 Ton That Dam, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A gritty, atmospheric old apartment block (the original 'cafe apartment', predating the famous 42 Nguyen Hue one) whose maze of corridors hides cool cafes, hipster bars and boutiques. A raw, architecturally fascinating dive into old-Saigon apartment life.

sights.address: Le Thanh Ton & Thai Van Lung, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A compact 'Little Tokyo' of lantern-hung alleys around Le Thanh Ton and Thai Van Lung, home to 300+ Japanese expats and a dense cluster of izakayas, ramen shops and karaoke bars. A miniature Japan in the heart of District 1, best after dark.

sights.address: 66 Ton That Thiep, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A colourful late-19th-century Hindu temple built by Saigon's Tamil community and dedicated to Lord Murugan, one of only three Hindu temples left in the city. A vivid, incense-filled surprise on a quiet downtown lane.

sights.address: 116A Hung Vuong, Ward 9, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A twin-spired Gothic church built 1922-1928 at the Nga Sau six-way roundabout, one of the city's most ornate ecclesiastical buildings and among the largest churches in Cho Lon. A striking, off-circuit alternative to Notre-Dame.

sights.address: 132-134 Dong Khoi, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The city's oldest hotel (1880) on former Rue Catinat opposite the Opera House, where Graham Greene wrote much of 'The Quiet American' in Room 214 and its terrace was the correspondents' 1950s watering hole. A living piece of literary and war-era Saigon.

sights.address: 01 Dong Khoi, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A 1925 French-colonial landmark on the Dong Khoi/Ton Duc Thang riverfront corner, built by the tycoon Hui Bon Hoa and preserving its original Art Deco character. Worth a look for the facade and a drink at its river-view rooftop.

sights.address: 141 Nguyen Hue, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The open-air rooftop bar of the 1960 Rex Hotel, site of the US military's daily wartime press briefings mocked as the 'Five O'Clock Follies'. Iconic Vietnam-War history plus sweeping views over Nguyen Hue and City Hall.

sights.address: 65 Le Loi, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The city's most polished shopping complex on Le Loi, anchored by Vietnam's first Takashimaya Japanese department store with a top-floor food court and basement Japanese supermarket. A cool, glossy contrast to the street markets.

sights.address: 3 Hoa Binh, Ward 3, District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A 50-hectare cultural-and-amusement park in District 11 with landscaped gardens, thrill rides, cultural exhibits and an adjoining water park. One of the city's big family day-outs, alongside Suoi Tien and Dai Nam.

sights.address: BB4, 188 Nguyen Van Huong, Thao Dien Ward, District 2 (Thu Duc City), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The live-jazz club of celebrated saxophonist Tran Manh Tuan, blending fusion and traditional jazz with Vietnamese folk influences; nightly sets from ~21:00. Recently relocated from downtown to Thao Dien; the city's premier jazz institution.
